contexts: A node-based compositing tool for visual effects (read, colour-correct, key, blur, merge nodes) whose artists tweak parameters interactively and whose final frames are rendered on a farm of many machines.
A WebGPU shader-graph material editor in the browser that must decide which shader variants to compile, cache and reuse as users edit material graphs.

questions.q1: Why must every field be length-prefixed before hashing?
questions.q2: Is the node id alone a sufficient cache key for evaluated results? If not, what must be added?
questions.q3: What can keys built from input keys not do when a change below produces identical pixels, and what mechanism is suggested if it matters?
questions.q4: How is a graph sent to another process, and how does the receiver arrive at the same ids?
questions.q5: What is the maximum number of entries in the originating project's result cache?
